jobs.title: Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
jobs.description:
CONTEXT

At Make-A-Wish® Canada
, we’re redefining how the world perceives wishes through our transformative new brand platform: Wishes Are Medicine.
Grounded in research, this platform recognizes what we’ve long known to be true — that wishes have measurable healing power. When prescribed alongside medical treatment, wishes reduce stress, elevate endorphins, limit emergency room visits, and deliver lasting health benefits.
With more than 3,500 children still waiting
and a new child diagnosed with a critical illness in Canada every two hours, our mission has never been more urgent — and there are many more prescriptions to fill.
To meet this challenge, we’ve launched our new three-year strategic plan — Wishes Are Medicine: One Team, One Mission
— focused intentionally on financial sustainability, mission impact, and operational excellence. When a child is facing a critical illness, a wish isn’t just a moment of joy — it’s a medically supported turning point. Studies show that children who receive a wish are 2.5 times less likely
to have unplanned hospital visits and 1.9 times less likely
to need the ER, with 100% of physicians agreeing that a wish can be a pivotal moment in treatment.
At Make-A-Wish Canada, you can play a lead role in bringing these powerful prescriptions to life. Where Wishes Are Medicine
, transformation becomes a pathway to healing at scale — and this role is your opportunity to architect that future.
Our ambition to reach more children and families requires a strong financial and operational foundation. As Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
, you will help shape that foundation, bringing strategic leadership to financial planning, investments, risk, governance and the services that enable our organization to thrive. You will turn insight into action, strengthen how resources are invested and managed, and help build a more resilient, disciplined and mission-driven organization.
At Make-A-Wish Canada
, you’ll join a team united by a shared mission and an unwavering sense of possibility. Every role — whether advancing fundraising, brand, operations, or technology — helps fuel the same trajectory: transforming how hope and healing come to life for children and families nationwide. If you’re ready to help build a future where every eligible child receives the wish that helps them heal, we invite you to read on.

ROLE OVERVIEW

We’re seeking a Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
, a strategic and forward-thinking leader who will help shape the next chapter of Make-A-Wish Canada. This is more than a finance role; it’s an opportunity to strengthen the financial and operational foundation that will enable our mission to grow sustainably.
As a key member of our Senior Leadership Team, and reporting to the Senior Vice President, Transformation & Operations, you will bring together financial strategy, business operations, analytics, risk and governance to strengthen how we plan, invest and make decisions. You’ll provide the insight and discipline to steward our resources responsibly, improve organizational performance, and build the capabilities needed to support sustainable growth and greater mission impact.
If you bring financial acumen, business curiosity and enterprise thinking, and believe the strongest organizations pair ambition with discipline, this is your opportunity to help build the foundation from which our mission can grow and bring the power of Wishes Are Medicine to more children and families across Canada.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Shape Financial Strategy:
Lead budgeting, forecasting, multi-year financial planning, and financial modelling. Translate insights into scenarios and recommendations that guide sustainable, mission-aligned decisions over a three-to-five-year time horizon.
Steward Assets and Investments:
Oversee financial assets, treasury, and investment portfolio performance in accordance with policy, ensuring disciplined stewardship and informed decision-making.
Strengthen Governance and Reporting:
Provide clear financial reporting to the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership Team, support the Finance & Audit Committee, and ensure sound governance, audit readiness, and compliance with CRA and other regulatory obligations.
Advance Enterprise Risk Management:
Maintain the enterprise risk register, strengthen internal controls, and lead business continuity and disaster recovery planning to protect the organization’s assets, reputation, and long-term sustainability.
Modernize Financial Capability:
Build stronger modelling, analytics, systems, and processes that improve forecasting, performance visibility, operational efficiency, and organizational decision-making.
Lead Business Services:
Oversee property management, leases, contracts, insurance, and related business services. Balance operational efficiency and financial sustainability with investments in organizational capability and a safe, supportive workplace.
Oversee Gift and Donation Administration:
Ensure sound systems and processes for restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex giving structures, coordinating closely with development teams to support stewardship and compliance.
Advise and Partner:
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Senior Vice President, Transformation & Operations, the CEO, and leadership colleagues on finance, risk, and business operations. Bring an enterprise lens to strategic planning and execution.
Guide and Develop Talent:
Build, coach, and lead a high-performing Finance and Business Operations team, creating clarity, accountability, collaboration, and opportunities for growth.
Champion One Team Leadership:
Model One Team, One Mission leadership by working across functions and geographies, breaking down silos, celebrating collective wins, and leading with empathy, inclusion, accountability, and purpose.
Represent the Mission:
Act as a visible and trusted ambassador with auditors, advisors, donors, partners, community leaders, and other stakeholders, supporting the Foundation’s presence and mission across Canada.

WHAT YOU BRING

You’re a strategic finance leader who pairs sound technical judgment with business curiosity and a hands-on approach. You move with ease between long-term vision and operational detail, helping leaders see the story behind the numbers and make bold, disciplined choices that bring the power of wishes to more children.
Proven Financial Leadership:
10+ years of progressive leadership in nonprofit financial management, with a track record of stewarding complex budgets, investments, assets, and financial operations in service of a bigger mission.
Strategic Insight:
Demonstrated strength in financial planning, forecasting, scenario analysis, and investment and treasury management, building the modelling capability that connects strategy, data, and execution.
Strong Credentials:
A CPA designation, supported by a bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business, or a related field, equipping you to lead with rigour and credibility.
Governance and Compliance Expertise:
Advanced knowledge of nonprofit financial management, CRA requirements, GAAP, audits, internal controls, insurance, and board and committee governance — the discipline that protects trust in our mission.
Enterprise Risk and Business Operations Excellence:
Experience in enterprise risk management, business continuity, procurement, contracts, property, insurance, and service delivery across a national or multi-site organization, building a resilient foundation for growth.
Gift Administration Knowledge:
Experience overseeing restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex donation structures, with a deep understanding of donor stewardship and the financial processing that honours every gift.
Collaborative People Leadership:
A track record of recruiting, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams, building trust across functions and rallying people around shared goals.
Clear and Credible Communication:
The ability to turn complex financial and risk information into practical insight for executives, board members, auditors, volunteers, donors, and cross-functional partners.
Inspiring, Values-Driven Leadership:
Deep alignment with our mission and a commitment to responsible stewardship, inclusion, and collaboration — a spirit that motivates teams, breaks down silos, and creates life-changing experiences for children and families facing critical illnesses.

HOW TO APPLY

If everything you’ve read so far sounds like you, we encourage you to apply
. Please visit the Make-A-Wish Canada candidate portal for current posting details and the application deadline.
Make-A-Wish Canada
provides equal opportunity in employment and encourages applications from all qualified candidates. Reasonable accommodations due to disability are available on request at any stage of the hiring process.

OUR COMMITMENT TO IDEA

Make-A-Wish Canada is committed to Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Access (IDEA)
. We believe it is essential to our mission that we build a diverse, balanced, and vibrant workforce that reflects the communities we serve and seek to serve. Research has shown that candidates from underrepresented groups often apply only when they feel 100% qualified. Even if you do not see yourself fully reflected in every requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

Once applications are reviewed, shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Our typical process includes a phone screen, one or two interviews, reference checking, an offer, and a criminal background check for the successful candidate. We thank all applicants for their interest in working with us.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Data Value
jobs.description:
Government Digital Service

Location Bristol, London, Manchester

Job grade SCS Pay Band 1

Contract type Permanent

Working pattern Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time, Compressed hours

Salary £86,000 - £117,800

Closing date Mon 30 Nov 2026

Reference 489478

Profession Digital, Information Technology

Apply now

You'll build a clear, trusted view of where data is making a difference across government and where it isn't, so leaders can choose with evidence instead of anecdote.

Why now?

AI is raising the stakes on data, and leaders need to know where their investment will pay off. At the moment there is no single, agreed way to show that across government.

We need one answer to a simple question. What is data worth to citizens, to services, to the economy and to national security? Then we need to use that answer to make better decisions.

It can be done. Others have already published practical guides to valuing data, covering how to take stock of it, assess it and put a value on it. We want to do the same, properly, for government.

Where you'll work

You'll be part of the Government Digital Service (GDS), the digital centre of government. We're home to GOV.UK and the Incubator for AI (i.AI), we lead the Government Digital and Data function, and we have more than 1,000 colleagues across London, Bristol and Manchester.

Job Description

What you'll do

Take stock of what government owns. Oversee a joined-up view of public data assets, including inventories, asset intelligence and valuation. Start with the assets that matter most to national infrastructure, public services and citizen-facing products.
Build the yardstick. Set up methods to judge the potential and the realised value of data assets and data-enabled products across their whole life, including where revenue could safely be raised to support public services.
Be the authority on 'value'. Decide what counts as data value, from economic and operational to assurance and risk reduction, and make it consistent and comparable across departments and portfolios. Advise senior leaders on how value is understood, evidenced and explained.
Show where it's working. Use that evidence to see where data creates the most value and where attention or investment should go next.
Help leaders make the call. Give senior decision-makers value-led evidence on priorities, sequencing and investment, so they can see what to scale, redirect, pause or stop. Base it on the whole system, not on one success story.
Keep citizens and users in the room. Make sure their view is built into every prioritisation and investment decision, working closely with Product, Portfolio and Strategy colleagues.
Follow the value through. Build value into decisions before, during and after delivery. Track how it changes over time, from performance and adoption to longer-term outcomes, and feed what you learn back into future choices.
Work safely in sensitive places. Operate within legislative, regulatory, governance and national security frameworks. Make visible the value that data brings in national security settings, where it often shows up as assurance, resilience or reduced risk.
Tell the story. Turn complex activity across government into clear, credible insight for senior leaders, and help the organisation move from one-off case studies to a system-level view of impact.
Lead a rigorous team. Lead the teams and partners working on data value, insight and asset intelligence, set a high bar for quality and professionalism, and help build a culture where decisions follow evidence.
One boundary. You provide evidence and analysis for commissioning, roadmap and portfolio discussions. You don't own delivery or benefits realisation in departments.

What Success Looks Like

A clear, trusted view of data value across government, built on comparable evidence of use, adoption, outcomes and benefits. Senior leaders can see where data is delivering and where they need to step in.
One system-wide definition of public value from data, covering citizen, service, economic and national outcomes, that shapes priorities, architecture and product decisions.
Valuation methods that let leaders compare data assets and products and decide when to scale, invest, pause or close.
A lifecycle approach, so value shapes decisions before, during and after delivery and feeds the next round of strategy, architecture and product priorities.
A story that senior leaders believe, moving us from one-off case studies to a system-level understanding of impact.

The honest bit

Valuing data across a whole government is hard, and the method is still being built. You'll be setting it up as well as using it, so expect plenty of debate about what counts as value and who decides.

Person specification

This role is for you if...

Role

You've helped very senior people make big decisions using data and evidence, and you can tell the difference between being busy and making a difference. You'll thrive in this role if you have:

Treated data as a strategic asset at a senior level, shaped how it is valued and accessed, and influenced decisions across a portfolio, a system or a whole organisation.
Used evidence to help senior leaders decide. You've brought information together from many sources to guide priorities, sequencing and investment in complicated settings.
Shown sharp analytical judgement. You can tell delivery activity, adoption and real outcomes apart, and you don't mistake progress for impact.
Influenced senior stakeholders by turning complex data, analysis or performance information into clear insight that makes trade-offs and risk-aware decisions easier.
Worked in governed, risk-aware settings, such as legislative, regulatory, assurance or security-sensitive ones, and understand that value can show up as assurance, resilience or reduced risk as well as delivery.
Worked across boundaries and in ambiguity, bringing policy, delivery, technical and operational teams together around one view of performance and value.

Bonus points

You're curious. You've taught yourself something, built something or written about something, at work or in your own time, and you'd enjoy telling us about it.

Apply now

The profession has technical specialists of all levels and backgrounds. They share a commitment to put users first and deliver world-leading government products and services.

Job roles within the profession range from trainee to Senior Civil Servants who lead on the very future of government itself.

Working in Government Digital and Data

Building the government of tomorrow

The UK government is recognised as a global leader in digital transformation. Government Digital and Data experts design, build and manage essential services that impact millions of peoples lives daily.

With an unprecedented number of digital transformation projects underway, the potential to help solve complex problems and shape our society’s future is enormous.

Examples Of Government Digital And Data Roles

User Researcher
Test Engineer
Content Designer
Software Developer
Delivery Manager
Business Analyst
DevOps Engineer
Product Manager
Infrastructure Engineer
Technical Architect

As a Government Digital and Data specialist you will be working at the cutting edge of how people interact, and are empowered by government.

You’ll work in collaborative multidisciplinary teams on a range of projects and services that focus on user needs and deliver real value to society. You’ll be part of a cross-government profession with clearly defined career paths, support and learning and development.
